g.text: Monorepo — circuit decomposition and snapshot lifetime
End without circuit changes
no
Runnable text recipe, classified embedding, positive dimensions?
Deduplicate in-range tokenizer entities
retain first available canonical placement per entity
At least two distinct entities?
no
Open model content snapshot
require snapshot source ID to equal admitted source
Own snapshot through reference-counted apply envelope
attach VerifySourceId callback
Native contraction computes salience and ordering
Check returned cardinality and index bounds
Pack ordered entity IDs and salience
centroid uses first at most 64 available placement anchors
StageCircuit identity from witness + model-circuit + plane
plus layer / head path components when present
Attach Projection physicality containing ordered token trajectory
Yield circuit change with retained snapshot envelope
Emit significant claim pages
each also retains snapshot envelope
yes
Circuit descriptor remains?
no
Update observed peak native resident bytes
yes
Relation family remains?
no
Log forms, significant claims, skipped circuits
and raw_weight_bytes_retained = 0
Dispose iterator's snapshot owner
emitted envelopes retain their own lifetime
IDENTITY DIFFERENCE: Wiki 24.6 identifies a circuit by its coupled content.
This source identifies it by witness and structural plane/layer/head address;
ordered coupled entities are stored in its Projection physicality.
Equal circuits in different source witnesses do not converge by this construction.
Source-reviewed orchestration. Nested semantics remain open; no runtime acceptance
claimed. Complete EmitAsync, BuildCircuitObservation and ModelCoordinates reviewed. Array
cardinality and index ranges are checked; permutation uniqueness is not checked here.
Native contraction, ModelCircuitEstate and apply-envelope implementation remain nested.
Yielding a retained envelope is not proof that every writer calls its verifier. This
source has no whole-checkpoint acceptance read. Logged raw retained bytes is a source
assertion, not an independent storage measurement.
